skill.description: 当用户需要做 X / Twitter 内容研究、账号作品观察、账号发出的回复分析、竞品内容对比或趋势判断时使用。区分账号主动参与的讨论与帖子收到的评论，保留可追溯的内容证据。
skill.summary: Research X topics, account posts, and outgoing replies with traceable evidence through SocialDataX.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: Two command sections instruct automatic execution of an unpinned npm package, creating dependency integrity risk under the agent's permissions. Other flags concern Markdown, normal credential configuration, official service links, a loopback proxy, or readable Chinese text. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, host reconnaissance, encoded payloads, or prompt injection in the supplied files; external package implementation was not supplied.

remediation.issue: CLI examples automatically execute socialdatax-skills@latest through npx -y.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version, verify package integrity, and obtain user approval before downloading or executing it. Use an isolated environment with limited credentials.

content.user_title: Research X Posts and Account Discussions
content.value_statement: X research can confuse account posts, outgoing replies, and incoming comments. This skill guides SocialDataX queries and organizes traceable evidence for focused content analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guides keyword searches and account lookups by username, user ID, or profile URL through SocialDataX CLI or corresponding MCP tools.
Retrieves account posts and outgoing replies as distinct research sources.
Organizes samples by topic while preserving returned links, timestamps, and visible context.
Continues paginated retrieval within user limits and preserves partial results after failures.
Guides user-requested media downloads from returned media URLs to a local directory.
Separates quoted account statements from analytical judgments and identifies missing fields.
limitations: Research queries require SocialDataX access, a configured API key, and sufficient service balance.
Direct CLI execution requires Node.js, npm, network access, and permission to run an external package.
The supplied files contain instructions, not the CLI implementation; external package behavior is outside this review.
Results may be partial or omit fields; small samples cannot establish complete relationships, private views, or comprehensive trends.

use_cases.title: Find Topic Angles
use_cases.description: Search a topic, group relevant samples, and retain evidence links for an editorial brief.

use_cases.title: Compare Account Content
use_cases.description: Compare specified accounts using separate post and outgoing-reply samples with explicit retrieval limits.

use_cases.title: Study Public Participation
use_cases.description: Identify discussions an account joins through its outgoing replies without treating incoming comments as account statements.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Search X for [topic] using one page. Summarize the main angles and include returned source links. Mark missing fields.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a bounded keyword research task.

prompt_templates.title: Review Account Posts
prompt_templates.prompt: Review one page of posts from [username]. Group themes and preserve returned links and timestamps. Separate evidence from interpretation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: examine an account's published content.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Outgoing Replies
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze outgoing replies from [profile URL], using at most two pages. Group discussion topics and quote representative evidence. Exclude incoming comments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: study account participation rather than audience responses.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Accounts with Recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare posts and outgoing replies for [account A] and [account B]. Limit each list to two pages. Preserve evidence and partial results. Resume only with matching continuation tokens. Report sample limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare accounts while maintaining separate pagination and recovery boundaries.

output_examples.input: Illustrative format: summarize one page of keyword results.
output: Scope: one returned page; broader coverage is not established.
Topic: [theme supported by the retrieved samples].
Observation: [interpretation tied to the cited evidence]. Missing fields: [fields not returned].

output_examples.input: Illustrative format: identify discussions an account joins.
output: Source: outgoing replies from [account], not comments received on its posts.
Discussion: [topic]. Account statement: [quoted reply]. Evidence: [returned reply link].
Coverage: [retrieved sample count]. Partial results and retrieval errors: [reported status].
Boundary: this sample does not establish complete relationships or private views.

best_practices: Specify the account, content type, and retrieval limits before requesting additional pages.
Preserve returned links, timestamps, and context; label missing fields and separate quotations from analysis.
Review and pin the external CLI package before execution, protect the API key, and approve dependency changes explicitly.
anti_patterns: Treating comments received on a post as replies authored by the account.
Inferring complete relationships or private views from a small or incomplete sample.
Restarting partial retrieval from the first page or repeatedly retrying an insufficient balance error.

faq.question: What access is required?
faq.answer: Research queries require a SocialDataX API key and service balance. Direct CLI usage also requires Node.js, npm, network access, and execution permission.

faq.question: Does the skill post or modify an X account?
faq.answer: The documented workflow excludes login, posting, likes, comments, and account changes. Optional media downloads write files locally.

faq.question: How are posts, replies, and comments different?
faq.answer: Posts are account publications. Outgoing replies are responses authored by that account. Comments are responses received on a particular post.

faq.question: Can I identify an account without its username?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented account queries accept a username, user ID, or profile URL as alternative selectors.

faq.question: What happens when retrieval is incomplete?
faq.answer: The workflow preserves retrieved items and errors. It resumes with a matching nonempty continuation token while retaining the original retrieval limits.

faq.question: Can I save returned media?
faq.answer: Yes, through the documented download command and a chosen local directory. Media downloads do not require the API key, but may need a proxy.
